title: Bitcoin Plummets Below $57K, Erasing $2.4 Billion in Crypto Bets【CoinDesk】
body:
Bitcoin’s price slipped beneath the $57,000 mark on Friday, settling around $56,300 – a level not seen since September 2024. The drop erased roughly $2.4 billion in open‑interest across futures and options contracts, intensifying a broader sell‑off that has already battered equities, commodities and other high‑risk assets. Traders and investors now face a stark reminder that the cryptocurrency’s two‑year rally may be far from over, and that market sentiment can turn sharply in response to macro‑economic pressures and regulatory uncertainty.

The slide came amid a confluence of factors that have been weighing on risk‑on assets throughout the week. U.S. Treasury yields continued to climb, pushing the 10‑year benchmark above 4.6 percent and reinforcing expectations of tighter monetary policy. At the same time, the Federal Reserve’s latest minutes hinted at a possible acceleration of rate hikes if inflation proves stubborn, prompting investors to retreat to safer havens such as the U.S. dollar and Treasury bonds. Bitcoin, long regarded as a “digital gold” hedge against fiat devaluation, appears to be losing its appeal in a climate where traditional safe assets are offering higher yields with less volatility.

Technical indicators also painted a bleak picture. The cryptocurrency’s price broke below the 200‑day moving average, a key support level that many analysts view as a barometer of long‑term trend strength. Momentum oscillators turned negative, and the relative strength index (RSI) dipped into oversold territory, suggesting that short‑term traders may be exiting positions en masse. Moreover, the open‑interest data released by major exchanges showed that leveraged bets on Bitcoin’s upside have been unwound at a rapid pace, contributing to the $2.4 billion erosion in derivatives exposure. This unwind is typical of a market that is transitioning from bullish optimism to caution, as participants seek to limit potential losses amid heightened uncertainty.

The broader cryptocurrency ecosystem felt the ripple effects. Ethereum (ETH) slipped below $1,800, while altcoins with higher volatility, such as Solana and Avalanche, posted double‑digit percentage declines. Institutional investors, who have been gradually increasing exposure to digital assets through custodial services and regulated funds, appear to be re‑evaluating their risk appetite. Some fund managers have publicly warned that “the macro backdrop is now the dominant driver of crypto performance,” underscoring a shift away from the narrative that Bitcoin’s price is primarily driven by its own network fundamentals.

Regulatory developments added another layer of complexity. In the United States, the Securities and Exchange Commission is expected to release new guidance on cryptocurrency derivatives later this month, a move that could tighten reporting requirements and potentially limit the availability of leveraged products. Meanwhile, Europe’s Markets in Crypto‑Assets (MiCA) framework is moving toward final implementation, promising greater consumer protection but also imposing stricter compliance burdens on exchanges. These policy signals have historically prompted market participants to adopt a defensive stance, especially when the regulatory trajectory is perceived as tightening.

Looking ahead, analysts are divided on whether Bitcoin can reclaim the $60,000 threshold that has acted as a psychological ceiling in recent weeks. Some technologists argue that the price correction is a healthy “reset” that will lay the groundwork for a more sustainable uptrend, especially if inflation eases and central banks adopt a more dovish stance. Others caution that continued pressure on risk assets, combined with the potential for further regulatory constraints, could keep Bitcoin trapped in a prolonged consolidation zone well into 2025. For now, market participants will be watching key support levels at $55,000 and $52,000, while keeping an eye on macro indicators such as U.S. employment data and global monetary policy decisions that could dictate the next direction of the crypto market.
